react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on a single dominant biological theme: tryptophan metabolism. Across four independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct pathway activity — the pathway "Tryptophan metabolism" (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465) achieved rank 1 with overwhelming statistical significance (FDR ≈ 3.4×10⁻¹⁵; p = 5.4×10⁻⁹). The RaMP ORA additionally identified "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and "Biogenic amine synthesis" (WP:WP550) as sub-pathway hits. The driver metabolites are precisely the six indolyl intermediates of the canonical tryptophan-to-serotonin-to-melatonin cascade: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). Notably, L-tryptophan was the sole substrate, while 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) independently flagged Vitamin A metabolism (rank 2, p=0.083) and molybdenum (C00150) showed no pathway membership, suggesting they are peripheral or treatment-specific non-metabolic hits. 3-Aminopropanal (C05665) appeared in histidine/beta-alanine metabolism (p<0.05) but with only two metabolites, a weaker signal than the tryptophan axis. The cross-paradigm consensus establishes that the treatment perturbation centres on tryptophan catabolism, with broad implications for neurochemical (serotonin), neuroendocrine (melatonin), and immunometabolic (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid / NAD⁺) homeostasis.

final_claims.claim_text: RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (FDR 3.44e-15) as the top pathway, hitting six compounds: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, with fold enrichment of 750.6.
The same six compounds were confirmed as members of the WikiPathways counterpart WP:WP465 (FDR 4.10e-15).
Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.59e-08) emerged as secondary enriched functions.
Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550, FDR 3.98e-08) emerged as secondary enriched functions.
MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned hsa00380 as the top pathway (p = 5.41e-09), matching the identical six compounds.
Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human metabolic network confirmed tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (p = 0.00227) with 13 of 14 pathway metabolites overlapping.
L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the substrate entry point in tryptophan metabolism.
Serotonin (KEGG:C00780) is a downstream product of tryptophan metabolism.
Melatonin (KEGG:C01598) is a downstream product of tryptophan metabolism.
Tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) is a downstream product of tryptophan metabolism.
L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the upstream substrate driving signal across the tryptophan metabolism pathway.

react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite panel was enriched for tryptophan metabolism across all three analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA returned KEGG:map00380 (FDR 3.44e-15) as the top pathway, hitting six compounds: L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, with fold enrichment of 750.6. The same six compounds were confirmed as members of the WikiPathways counterpart WP:WP465 (FDR 4.10e-15). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 3.59e-08) and Biogenic amine synthesis (WP:WP550, FDR 3.98e-08) emerged as secondary enriched functions. Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human metabolic network confirmed tryptophan metabolism as the top hit (p = 0.00227) with 13 of 14 pathway metabolites overlapping. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently returned hsa00380 as the top pathway (p = 5.41e-09), matching the identical six compounds. L-Tryptophan (KEGG:C00078) is the substrate entry point; serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), and tryptamine (KEGG:C00398) are downstream products of parallel branch points in the pathway. The convergence across ORA, network, and PSEA paradigms establishes tryptophan metabolism as the primary affected system.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolites converge on a single dominant biological theme: tryptophan metabolism. Across four independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-direct pathway activity — the pathway "Tryptophan metabolism" (KEGG:hsa00380 / WP:WP465) achieved rank 1 with overwhelming statistical significance (FDR ≈ 3.4×10⁻¹⁵; p = 5.4×10⁻⁹). The RaMP ORA additionally identified "Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis" (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and "Biogenic amine synthesis" (WP:WP550) as sub-pathway hits. The driver metabolites are precisely the six indolyl intermediates of the canonical tryptophan-to-serotonin-to-melatonin cascade: L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), tryptamine (C00398), indoleacetaldehyde (C00637), serotonin (C00780), melatonin (C01598), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632). Notably, L-tryptophan was the sole substrate, while 4-hydroxyretinoic acid (C16677) independently flagged Vitamin A metabolism (rank 2, p=0.083) and molybdenum (C00150) showed no pathway membership, suggesting they are peripheral or treatment-specific non-metabolic hits. 3-Aminopropanal (C05665) appeared in histidine/beta-alanine metabolism (p<0.05) but with only two metabolites, a weaker signal than the tryptophan axis. The cross-paradigm consensus establishes that the treatment perturbation centres on tryptophan catabolism, with broad implications for neurochemical (serotonin), neuroendocrine (melatonin), and immunometabolic (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid / NAD⁺) homeostasis.
